title: Man shot by cops dies ; 43-year-old 'interacted' with police after high-speed chase, shooting of denturist
article: The 43-year-old man shot by Ottawa police along Hwy. 417 Wednesday evening died in hospital yesterday, according to Ontario's Special Investigations Unit.
Richard Bastien died shortly after 10 a.m. An autopsy will be conducted this morning.
Police shot him after a highway chase through rush-hour traffic that ended near Walkley Rd.

Bastien, who is from Montreal, got out of the car and "interacted" with three officers before producing a handgun, the SIU said. An officer fired a number of shots and Bastien was struck once in the chest.
Police had been pursuing the car in connection with an attempted murder investigation at a Carp-area home, where 65-year-old Rainer Elsner was shot multiple times.
Elsner was shot in the head, back and arm. He was still recovering from his injuries yesterday in hospital.
Neighbour Jean-Claude Hubert said Bastien was an employee of Elsner's for the past six years at the denture business he operated out of his Carp-area home.
Hubert said Elsner ran over to his house Wednesday screaming he had been shot and was bleeding down his arms. Elsner was turning white and in shock, Hubert said.
Hubert said Elsner called him Sunday saying Bastien had robbed him of more than $20,000. Elsner alleged Bastien forged cheques while he was on vacation in Germany recently.
"He said: 'I trusted him. He was a friend and he stole my money," Hubert said of the telephone conversation with Elsner.
According to the account Elsner gave Hubert after he was shot, Bastien had come to see him about the missing money, but Elsner refused to talk about it because it was in the hands of police.
That's when Bastien is alleged to have pulled out a gun and shot Elsner three times.
